title: How Long Does It Take to Automate Finance in Practice?
summary: See how long it takes to automate finance end to end and which factors speed up or delay the implementation.
body_markdown:
The time to automate finance end to end usually ranges from a few days to a few weeks, depending on how complex the flow is and how many systems need to connect. A simple accounts payable approval flow can be ready in days; a process with multiple cost centers, authorization levels, and ERP integration may need more design time before it goes live.


This question comes up because growing companies feel finance getting stuck: approvals take too long, entries pile up, and the team spends hours copying data between spreadsheets, email, and the ERP. End to end means covering everything from the initial request to the posting in the financial system, with no manual step in between.


The real timeline depends less on the tool and more on how clear the process is: if the approval rules, authorization levels, and cost centers are already defined, the automation comes together fast. If they're still only in one person's head, mapping the process takes more time than the technical setup itself.


## What Usually Delays Finance Automation


- Approval rules that change depending on who's on vacation
- No standardized cost center across departments
- Parallel spreadsheets that nobody updates at the same time
- No clear definition of who approves each value range
- Dependence on email to authorize payments


## Steps of an End-to-End Finance Automation


- Map the current flow, from request to payment
- Define authorization levels by amount, cost center, or supplier
- Set up the request form or card
- Connect approval to automatic posting in the ERP
- Test exceptions (high amounts, new suppliers, urgent cases)
- Monitor the flow in production for a few weeks before expanding


## Factors That Speed Up This Implementation


- Having data already organized in a single table speeds up the start
- Multiple company IDs or ERP accounts require more design time
- Native ERP integration avoids manual export steps
- Teams with no documented process spend more time aligning rules before automating
